column3: It names the manifest loss of self and family at the Last Day, directly specifying the focus's double loss.

It gives a distinct case in which hostile planning ends in loss for its authors.

When provision is restricted, the same person says God has humiliated him, completing the adverse-outcome misreading absent from 89:15 alone.

After hardship, mercy leads a person to declare evil gone and become exultant, giving the favorable side of conditional response.

Once God removes harm, some associate partners, directly showing reversal after relief.
At sea danger people call only on God, then turn away when He saves them to land, a close rescue-and-reversal instance.
